disposition_vocabulary.rename: A full-word replacement is settled; the cluster worker applies it.
disposition_vocabulary.superseded: The column disappears with its table or is removed by another task; no rename.
disposition_vocabulary.blocked_operator_ruling: DEVIATION from the task plan, which specified only rename/keep/superseded. Used where a name cannot be settled without an operator decision. Folding these into `rename` would assert decisions this task was told not to make unilaterally.
disposition_vocabulary.keep: The name stands. Used only where a prior operator ruling conflicts with the audit rule; each keep REQUIRES a rule refinement in audit-schema-conformance.mjs or the gate cannot reach zero.

notes.boolean_overlap: ZERO. Not merely empirically -- structurally. audit-schema-conformance.mjs computes is_unprefixed_boolean BEFORE the shorthand block and the bare-short-name branch guards on !unprefixed_boolean, so a column cannot be reported under both rules. comm(1) over class-shorthand.txt and class-boolean-prefix.txt confirms an empty intersection. No column is double-scheduled and no marking was required.
notes.audit_rule_conflict: db/adhoc/2026-07-22-player-prospect-profile-sis-conform.sql:5 records the operator ruling "IQR kept (proprietary metric name, like EPA)" while conforming 224 SIS columns. audit-schema-conformance.mjs:148 says the opposite -- that domain acronyms including epa are "likewise not exempt". Six columns sit in that gap (epa on nfl_plays, nfl_plays_current_week and both player_college tables; iqr on both player_college tables). They are marked `keep` on the strength of the operator ruling, which outranks the script. The script needs epa and iqr added to its exempt set. Note the ruling does NOT extend to adp, faab or cpoe, which have unambiguous expansions and are mapped as renames.
notes.lifecycle: MIGRATION INSTRUMENT, NOT A PERMANENT ARTIFACT. It is authoritative input for the per-cluster migrations -- eleven workers consume it so they do not each re-derive the vocabulary and drift -- which is exactly why it cannot live under scratch/: user:guideline/scratch-tier-discipline.md states that scratch is never a source of truth and that "grepping scratch/ for authoritative answers is a workflow bug", and scratch is single-machine so it cannot cross hosts. Retirement trigger: when the audit's shorthand class reaches its floor of 29 (23 superseded + 6 keep) and those are cleared by their owning tasks, DELETE this file in the same commit that closes the class. The durable residue is not this JSON -- it is the applied db/adhoc/*.sql files, the schema itself, and the three non-obvious rulings recorded as observations on user:task/league/redesign-league-database-schema.md (pos -> player_position rather than the audit hint, the epa/iqr exemption, and the nine dead columns).
notes.output_path: This file sits under scratch/, which .gitignore excludes at rule `scratch/*/*/*`. The task plan says to COMMIT it; at this path that is impossible. Recommend relocating to repository/active/league/db/adhoc/shorthand-rename-map.json, beside the audit script that defines the rule it answers to.

NEVER FUNCTIONAL. Git archaeology: 5811f8ce4 ("feat: dashboard extension salary & savings", 2021-08-04) added ext1-4 to the league record in app/core/leagues/league.js, but only as destructured plumbing -- no calculation ever read them. Every later commit touching the name in libs-shared/, libs-server/, api/ or scripts/ is a refactor or migration (8c2320353 rename, dd04c20a6 data script, b324029ce leagues->seasons move), never a consumer. The live formula libs-shared/get-extension-amount.mjs:52 is `value + (extensions + 1) * 5`, a LINEAR +5/+10/+15/+20 ladder that has never matched the ext1-4 defaults of 5/10/20/35. All 122 season rows across 116 leagues carry the identical default (verified by query), the columns are absent from the settings allowlist in api/routes/leagues/league-settings.mjs so they cannot be set, the SPA exposes no extension-cost control, and libs-server/context-docs/generate-league-rules.mjs:132 publishes the rule as a flat "$5 over the prior season salary". These are speculative configurability that was never implemented, not a broken wiring to repair. If per-league extension pricing is wanted it is a NEW feature needing ladder semantics, settings API, SPA UI, rules-doc generation and a rule for the 5th extension (production rosters_players.extensions reaches 4, which a four-tier ladder does not cover) -- not a resurrection of these columns.

Settled against production across all 19 transaction types. Every type carries a dollar-salary distribution and none shows non-salary behaviour: ROSTER_RELEASE is 0 on all 2,481 rows (a released player carries no salary), FRANCHISE_TAG runs 10-47 matching the seasons.fqb/frb/fwr/fte tag prices, DRAFT runs 1-12 as rookie salary by pick, PRACTICE_ADD is 0-1, and TRADE tops out at 136 -- the SAME ceiling as ROSTER_ACTIVATE and RESERVE_IR, so trades carry the player's salary rather than any separate trade-value metric. That was the one gap that previously blocked this entry. Writers agree: libs-server/submit-acquisition.mjs:232, process-restricted-free-agency-bid.mjs:140, submit-activate.mjs:71, process-poach.mjs:123, api/routes/leagues/draft.mjs:384 ("value based on draft position for salary purposes"), process-release.mjs:304 (value 0). Named player_salary rather than bare `salary` so a grep returns its real uses, and rather than salary_value which is redundant.

Operator ruling 2026-08-04: drop, after verification. PROVENANCE: added by 9ac198280 ("feat: add manual and average starter value baselines", 2020-07-21) as a per-position manual baseline PLAYER reference; the whole feature was removed by 2d250a67c ("cleanup: remove manual baselines", 2022-07-15), which deleted every consumer and dropped the columns from the then-current MySQL schema file -- but the DROP was never run against the live database, so the Postgres dump re-materialised them. Pure leftover debt from a feature removed in 2022. VERIFIED DEAD three ways: (1) zero code references tree-wide including private/, db/migrations/ and db/fixtures/, with the search method proven first by positive control (invite_code 25 hits, username 192); (2) only 11 of 133 rows non-null, one of those four empty strings; (3) the stored values are player ids in a retired format (KA-0737, MB-3537) and ZERO resolve against the current player.pid scheme (ANTO-CRAW-000002). NOTE for the drop author: api/routes/me.mjs:175 issues a bare db('users').where(...) with no .select(), so these four columns are currently serialised into the /me response payload; nothing in app/core reads them, so removal is a payload shrink with no consumer impact, but the response shape does change.
